# Data Visualization Skill

Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.

## Chart Selection Guide

### Choose by Data Relationship

| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |

### When NOT to Use Certain Charts

- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.

## Python Visualization Code Patterns

### Setup and Style

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Professional style setup
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# Colorblind-friendly palettes
PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']
PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'
PALETTE_DIVERGING = 'RdBu_r'
```

### Line Chart (Time Series)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for label, group in df.groupby('category'):
    ax.plot(group['date'], group['value'], label=label, linewidth=2)

ax.set_title('Metric Trend by Category', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Date')
ax.set_ylabel('Value')
ax.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Format dates on x-axis
fig.autofmt_xdate()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('trend_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Bar Chart (Comparison)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Sort by value for easy reading
df_sorted = df.sort_values('metric', ascending=True)

bars = ax.barh(df_sorted['category'], df_sorted['metric'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0])

# Add value labels
for bar in bars:
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax.text(width + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{width:,.0f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=10)

ax.set_title('Metric by Category (Ranked)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Metric Value')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('bar_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Number Formatting Helpers

```python
def format_number(val, format_type='number'):
    """Format numbers for chart labels."""
    if format_type == 'currency':
        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
            return f'${val/1e9:.1f}B'
        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
            return f'${val/1e6:.1f}M'
        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
            return f'${val/1e3:.1f}K'
        else:
            return f'${val:,.0f}'
    elif format_type == 'percent':
        return f'{val:.1f}%'
    elif format_type == 'number':
        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
            return f'{val/1e9:.1f}B'
        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
            return f'{val/1e6:.1f}M'
        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
            return f'{val/1e3:.1f}K'
        else:
            return f'{val:,.0f}'
    return str(val)

# Usage with axis formatter
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format_number(x, 'currency')))
```

--- brief ---
# National Development Parallel Coordinates Dataset

## Overview
This dataset contains 30 countries spanning four World Bank income groups (High, Upper-Middle, Lower-Middle, Low) with seven development indicators, designed for a parallel coordinates visualization of multidimensional national profiles.

## Data Source

### national_development
Each record represents one country with the following fields:
- **country** (string): Country name
- **income_group** (string): World Bank income classification — one of High, Upper-Middle, Lower-Middle, Low
- **gdp_per_capita_usd** (numeric): GDP per capita in current USD, range ~380–87,720
- **hdi** (numeric): Human Development Index, range 0.394–0.961
- **freedom_index** (numeric): Freedom House aggregate score, 0–100 (100 = most free)
- **corruption_perceptions_index** (numeric): Transparency International CPI score, 0–100 (100 = least corrupt)
- **co2_emissions_per_capita_tons** (numeric): Annual CO₂ emissions in metric tons per capita, range 0.1–21.8
- **military_expenditure_pct_gdp** (numeric): Military spending as percentage of GDP, range 0.6–6.0
- **internet_penetration_pct** (numeric): Percentage of population using the internet, range 14–99

## Data Notes
- Values are approximate 2023 estimates compiled from World Bank, UNDP, Freedom House, Transparency International, IEA, SIPRI, and ITU.
- Income group assignments follow the World Bank July 2023 classification.
- Some values for conflict-affected states (e.g., Afghanistan) carry higher uncertainty.
- CO₂ figures are production-based and exclude land-use change emissions.

import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
from matplotlib import patheffects as pe

DATA_PATH = Path('/app/benchmark/source_data.json')
OUT_PATH = Path('/app/output/result.png')
OUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

with DATA_PATH.open() as f:
    raw = json.load(f)['national_development']['data']

df = pd.DataFrame(raw)

axes = [
    ('gdp_per_capita_usd', 'GDP per capita\n(USD, log scale)', 'currency_log'),
    ('hdi', 'Human Development\nIndex (0–1)', 'decimal'),
    ('freedom_index', 'Freedom Index\n(0–100, freer →)', 'integer'),
    ('corruption_perceptions_index', 'Corruption Perceptions\nIndex (0–100, cleaner →)', 'integer'),
    ('co2_emissions_per_capita_tons', 'CO₂ emissions\n(t/person/year)', 'decimal1'),
    ('military_expenditure_pct_gdp', 'Military spend\n(% of GDP)', 'percent1'),
    ('internet_penetration_pct', 'Internet penetration\n(% of population)', 'percent0'),
]

# Transform only for scale readability; tick labels remain original values.
def transform(series, kind):
    vals = series.astype(float).to_numpy()
    if kind == 'currency_log':
        return np.log10(vals)
    return vals

def inv_transform(vals, kind):
    vals = np.asarray(vals)
    if kind == 'currency_log':
        return 10 ** vals
    return vals

def fmt(value, kind):
    if kind == 'currency_log':
        if value >= 1000:
            return f'${value/1000:.0f}k'
        return f'${value:.0f}'
    if kind == 'decimal':
        return f'{value:.2f}'
    if kind == 'decimal1':
        return f'{value:.1f}'
    if kind == 'percent1':
        return f'{value:.1f}%'
    if kind == 'percent0':
        return f'{value:.0f}%'
    return f'{value:.0f}'

norm = pd.DataFrame(index=df.index)
axis_meta = {}
for col, label, kind in axes:
    transformed = transform(df[col], kind)
    mn, mx = transformed.min(), transformed.max()
    norm[col] = (transformed - mn) / (mx - mn)
    axis_meta[col] = {'min': mn, 'max': mx, 'kind': kind, 'label': label}

# Research/policy palette: high contrast, colorblind-conscious, not overly saturated.
colors = {
    'High': '#1B5EAA',
    'Upper-Middle': '#D9822B',
    'Lower-Middle': '#3C8D5A',
    'Low': '#7B4AB3',
}
order = ['High', 'Upper-Middle', 'Lower-Middle', 'Low']

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 10.5), dpi=180)
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#F7F8FA')
ax.set_facecolor('#F7F8FA')

x = np.arange(len(axes))

# Alternating panels to improve dense reading.
for i in range(len(axes) - 1):
    if i % 2 == 0:
        ax.axvspan(i, i + 1, color='#E9EDF3', alpha=0.42, zorder=0)

# Quantile ribbons and median traces for income-group bands.
for group in order:
    idx = df.index[df['income_group'] == group]
    values = norm.loc[idx, [a[0] for a in axes]].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    q1 = np.quantile(values, 0.25, axis=0)
    q3 = np.quantile(values, 0.75, axis=0)
    med = np.median(values, axis=0)
    ax.fill_between(x, q1, q3, color=colors[group], alpha=0.07, zorder=1, linewidth=0)
    ax.plot(x, med, color=colors[group], lw=3.2, alpha=0.85, zorder=3,
            path_effects=[pe.Stroke(linewidth=5.2, foreground='white', alpha=0.62), pe.Normal()])

# Country polylines. Draw less central profiles first; emphasize selected outliers.
highlight_countries = {
    'United Arab Emirates': 'High-income / very high CO₂ & military',
    'Saudi Arabia': 'High-income / low freedom, high CO₂',
    'Singapore': 'High-income / CPI high, freedom lower',
    'Russia': 'Upper-middle / low CPI, high military',
    'China': 'Upper-middle / low freedom, high CO₂',
    'India': 'Lower-middle / freedom above group peers',
    'Mali': 'Low-income / military share high',
}

# Plot non-highlighted lines.
for _, row in df[~df['country'].isin(highlight_countries)].iterrows():
    y = norm.loc[row.name, [a[0] for a in axes]].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ax.plot(x, y, color=colors[row['income_group']], lw=1.35, alpha=0.34, zorder=2)

# Plot highlighted lines on top.
for _, row in df[df['country'].isin(highlight_countries)].iterrows():
    y = norm.loc[row.name, [a[0] for a in axes]].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ax.plot(x, y, color=colors[row['income_group']], lw=2.8, alpha=0.98, zorder=5,
            path_effects=[pe.Stroke(linewidth=4.8, foreground='white', alpha=0.88), pe.Normal()])

# Vertical axes, original-value tick labels.
for i, (col, label, kind) in enumerate(axes):
    ax.vlines(i, 0, 1, color='#303845', lw=1.15, zorder=4)
    meta = axis_meta[col]
    tick_norms = np.linspace(0, 1, 5)
    tick_vals = inv_transform(meta['min'] + tick_norms * (meta['max'] - meta['min']), kind)
    for t, v in zip(tick_norms, tick_vals):
        ax.plot([i - 0.025, i + 0.025], [t, t], color='#303845', lw=0.85, zorder=6)
        ha = 'right' if i in [0, 1, 2] else 'left'
        dx = -0.045 if ha == 'right' else 0.045
        ax.text(i + dx, t, fmt(v, kind), ha=ha, va='center', fontsize=8.1, color='#2B3037', zorder=7)
    ax.text(i, 1.075, label, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10.5, fontweight='bold', color='#151B23')

# Highlight the freedom-CPI segment with an analytical annotation.
ax.axvspan(2, 3, color='#FFE8B3', alpha=0.24, zorder=0)
ax.text(2.5, -0.105, 'Freedom ↔ CPI cluster: many lines are near-parallel,\nwith autocracy/corruption crossovers visible in highlighted cases',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=9.4, color='#5A3A00',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.38', facecolor='#FFF4D6', edgecolor='#D8AE49', linewidth=0.8))

# Annotate selected outlier end/inflection points without overwhelming the dense chart.
annotations = [
    ('United Arab Emirates', 4, 0.16, 0.04),
    ('Saudi Arabia', 2, -0.17, -0.035),
    ('Singapore', 3, 0.12, 0.06),
    ('Russia', 5, 0.13, 0.035),
    ('China', 2, -0.12, 0.05),
    ('India', 2, -0.16, 0.055),
    ('Mali', 5, 0.12, -0.04),
]
for country, axis_idx, dx, dy in annotations:
    row_idx = df.index[df['country'] == country][0]
    col = axes[axis_idx][0]
    y = float(norm.loc[row_idx, col])
    group = df.loc[row_idx, 'income_group']
    ax.scatter([axis_idx], [y], s=38, color=colors[group], edgecolor='white', linewidth=1.0, zorder=8)
    ax.annotate(country, xy=(axis_idx, y), xytext=(axis_idx + dx, min(max(y + dy, 0.02), 0.98)),
                fontsize=8.3, color='#171B20', ha='left' if dx > 0 else 'right', va='center', zorder=9,
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color='#5E6673', lw=0.8, shrinkA=1, shrinkB=3),
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.22', facecolor='white', edgecolor='#D0D5DD', alpha=0.92, linewidth=0.7))

# Add small crossover markers for the steepest adjacent-axis changes.
changes = []
cols = [a[0] for a in axes]
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    vals = norm.loc[idx, cols].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    diffs = np.abs(np.diff(vals))
    for j, d in enumerate(diffs):
        changes.append((d, row['country'], j, vals[j], vals[j+1], row['income_group']))
for d, country, j, y0, y1, group in sorted(changes, reverse=True)[:12]:
    xm = j + 0.5
    ym = (y0 + y1) / 2
    ax.scatter([xm], [ym], marker='x', s=28, color=colors[group], linewidths=1.0, alpha=0.75, zorder=6)

ax.text(5.35, -0.105, '× marks steepest adjacent-axis rank shifts\n(non-linear crossover profiles)',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=9.2, color='#343A40')

legend_lines = [Line2D([0], [0], color=colors[g], lw=3, label=g) for g in order]
legend_bands = [Patch(facecolor='#6B7280', alpha=0.12, edgecolor='none', label='Income-group interquartile band')]
steep_marker = [Line2D([0], [0], marker='x', color='#343A40', lw=0, markersize=7, label='Steep adjacent-axis shift')]
leg = ax.legend(handles=legend_lines + legend_bands + steep_marker,
                loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.18), ncol=6,
                frameon=True, fancybox=False, framealpha=0.96, borderpad=0.75,
                title='World Bank income group')
leg.get_frame().set_edgecolor('#D0D5DD')
leg.get_title().set_fontweight('bold')

ax.set_title('National Development Profiles Across Seven Indicators',
             loc='left', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', color='#111827', pad=70)
ax.text(0, 1.165,
        'Parallel coordinates for 30 countries; each line is normalized per axis while tick labels show source units.\n'
        'Separation is strongest on GDP, HDI, internet access and CO₂, while freedom/CPI and military spending reveal crossovers and outlier profiles.',
        transform=ax.transData, ha='left', va='bottom', fontsize=11.2, color='#3E4652')

ax.set_xlim(-0.52, len(axes) - 0.48)
ax.set_ylim(-0.16, 1.22)
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_yticks([])
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

# Source note.
fig.text(0.012, 0.018,
         'Source: national_development dataset (approx. 2023 values from World Bank, UNDP, Freedom House, Transparency International, IEA, SIPRI, ITU).',
         ha='left', va='bottom', fontsize=8.5, color='#667085')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0.01, 0.04, 0.995, 0.955])
fig.savefig(OUT_PATH, dpi=180, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
plt.close(fig)
print(OUT_PATH)

ax.set_ylim(-0.16, 1.22)

ax.set_yticks([])
